# Specifying

## What it means

Specifying is the [pillar](./pillar.md) of writing down what is wanted, and agreeing it, before it is built. What is written is a [spec](./spec.md). A spec is optional. When work has a spec, the work is checked against it.

One thing about Specifying is fixed. When a unit of work is being specified, it has no [breakdown](./breakdown.md) until its spec is agreed, and its breakdown and its [acceptance criteria](./acceptance-criteria.md) are drawn from that spec. Everything else is a process that the Human Lead can change: what a spec must contain, who reviews it, what counts as agreed, and how criteria are written.

## Where it is kept

A spec that is not yet agreed is a [draft](./draft.md) in the Workbench. An [agreed spec](./agreed-spec.md) is in a publish area.

## What acts on it

With the default set, the process specify takes an idea to an agreed spec that is published. It uses the verb spec-draft to write the draft and the verb spec-agree to publish it. The core contract spec-before-breakdown guards this pillar.
